subject.title: [Bug]: Trajectory files fed back as context cause unbounded token consumption and unexpected API billing

question: Is source-level guardrail evidence enough to close this billing report, or should maintainers require an exact Windows/provider live proof first?
rationale: The code now has plausible protections, but the observed impact is high and the remaining uncertainty is proof sufficiency rather than a narrow confirmed implementation defect.

options.title: Require live proof before close
options.body: Keep this issue open until a maintainer or trusted tester proves the fresh-session path on current main with large trajectory sidecars.

options.title: Close from source guardrails
options.body: Close as fixed if maintainers accept the transcript, bootstrap, TUI, and reseed guardrails as sufficient despite missing exact billing-path proof.

options.title: Add another defensive guardrail
options.body: Keep open for a targeted patch only if review identifies a concrete remaining hook, memory, or reseed path that can still ingest trajectory sidecars.

recommendation.title: Require live proof before close
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open until a maintainer or trusted tester proves the fresh-session path on current main with large trajectory sidecars.

likelyOwner.reason: The most direct current-main guardrail evidence is in session artifact classification and trajectory-sidecar cleanup history.
